title: CORE ENGINE
why: 8 hours sleep and you want to push, but your legs are sore and you hammered them yesterday (heavy squats + hard intervals). So the push goes where you're fresh: a loaded core block and a redline anti-rotation finisher, plus steady Zone 2 running that doubles as active recovery for the legs. No heavy squats, no lunges, no high-impact intervals. This also fills your two biggest coverage gaps this week: core/midline and steady Zone 2.

blocks.title: WARM-UP
blocks.text: 3 min easy walk-to-jog (4.5 mph, loosen the sore legs) · Cat-cow ×8 · Thoracic rotations 6/side · Hip flexor rock 8/side · Deadbug 6/side · Bird-dog 6/side · 5 slow halos each way (16 kg) to wake the core.

blocks.title: LOADED CORE
blocks.text: Slow and heavy. Get-ups own your whole midline and spare the sore legs; windmills load anti-side-bend with light overhead (easy on the mildly sore arms); suitcase carry is pure anti-lean core and grip. 3 rounds solid, 4 if you're moving well. Nail every rep, no rush.

blocks.title: REDLINE CORE
blocks.text: This is your push. 12-minute AMRAP — flow through all four and keep score. Rows in a tight plank (anti-rotation, easy on the arms), twists and hollow rocks torch the midline, light swings keep the heart rate pinned and flush the legs. Redline it, but keep the plank honest — don't let the hips sag when you fatigue. Set the COUNTDOWN timer to 12:00.

blocks.title: STEADY ENGINE

items.name: Treadmill
items.detail: 16 min @ 6.5 mph (6.0 if legs are barking), 1-2% incline

blocks.text: Deliberately steady, not intervals. Your legs are sore, so this is easy aerobic work that pumps blood through them and actually speeds recovery for tomorrow. Nose-breathing pace, could hold a conversation. This is the steady Zone 2 you've been missing all week. If the legs feel great, hold 6.5; if they're barking, drop to 6.0 and just keep it smooth.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.text: Walk 2 min at 3 mph · Stretch 30s each: quads, hamstrings, hip flexors, glutes, calves (hit the sore legs) · Lat + thoracic opener · Child's pose 30s.
